descriptionChirho: A masculine noun denoting thorny bushes or brier plants, typically appearing in prophetic judgment contexts describing desolation and uncultivated land. All three clusters represent the same lexeme שַׁיִת in different syntactic frames: conjunctive (eng 'and briers', spa 'y cardos', hin और झाड़ी, arb وَالْحَسَكَ, kor 찌레가, swa 'na mbigili'), suffixed possessive (eng 'its thorns', spa 'su espino', hin उसकी झाड़ियों, arb شَوْكَهُ, kor 그 찌레와, swa 'mbigili yake'), and bare nominal (eng 'thorn', spa 'y cardos', hin झाड़ी, arb وَعَوْسَجَا, swa 'na michongoma'). Multilingual evidence uniformly points to thorny vegetation.
